sci-repo-y8-sby-2018-systems-mc-1.title: Year 8 Science — Body systems and reproduction — SafetyBay2018 (original source MC)
sci-repo-y8-sby-2018-systems-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is listed from simplest structure to the most complex structure?
questions.explanation: Cell→tissue→organ→system is increasing structural complexity.

questions.prompt: Which type of blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, regardless of oxygenation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are the smallest blood vessels?
questions.explanation: Capillaries are the smallest listed blood vessels.

questions.prompt: The lungs, nose, and trachea are a part of which system?
questions.explanation: Respiratory system.

questions.prompt: Which organ contains air-carrying tubes and tiny sacs?
questions.explanation: Lungs contain branching airways and alveoli.

questions.prompt: The offspring from an organism that reproduces asexually are
questions.explanation: Asexual offspring are typically genetically identical to each other except for mutations.

questions.prompt: An advantage of sexual reproduction is it
options: Occurs over a short period of time.
Has a low chance of survival.
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction increases genetic variation through recombination/segregation and fertilisation.

sci-repo-y9-sby-2017-endocrine-mc-1.title: Year 9 Science — Endocrine system and diseases — SafetyBay2017 (original source MC)
sci-repo-y9-sby-2017-endocrine-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: Name the hormone that helps control water levels in the blood.
questions.explanation: ADH helps regulate kidney water reabsorption and blood water balance.

questions.prompt: Which of these will be in the 1st line of defence?
questions.explanation: Skin is a first-line physical barrier.

questions.prompt: The role of the antibody is
options: Release a chemical that causes increased blood flow to the infected area
To cause the pathogens to clump together so macrophages can destroy more at one time
To activate the third line of defence
questions.explanation: C describes one antibody action: cross-linking/agglutination can aid clearance. Antibodies also neutralise and opsonise; they do not themselves engulf pathogens.

questions.prompt: Chemicals that cause your body to react as if it has met a pathogen before are called
questions.explanation: Vaccines safely expose the immune system to antigens or instructions for making them, priming protective memory.

questions.prompt: Penicillin is
questions.explanation: D is the intended historical answer: penicillin became the first widely successful therapeutic antibiotic. It is not an antiviral.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a white blood cell?
questions.explanation: An antibody is a protein, not a white blood cell.

questions.prompt: Diseases that are easiest to spread are known as
questions.explanation: Contagious describes infections readily transmitted between hosts; not all infectious diseases spread directly person-to-person.

sci-repo-y9-sby-2017-tectonics-mc-1.title: Year 9 Science — Plate tectonics — SafetyBay2017 (original source MC)
sci-repo-y9-sby-2017-tectonics-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: Which observation led to the hypothesis of seafloor spreading?
options: The claim of a large land mass referred to as Pangaea.
That there is a Global Rift system and undersea mountains.
Scientists in 1872 discovering a mountain ridge in the Atlantic Ocean.
The earth has several layers with different physical properties.
questions.explanation: B. Mid-ocean ridge/rift observations supported seafloor spreading, together with magnetic/age evidence.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a type of plate boundary?
questions.explanation: Continental is a crustal category, not one of the three principal plate-boundary types.

questions.prompt: List the order of colouring in magma as it begins to cool.
questions.explanation: D is the intended incandescent cooling sequence: white→yellow→orange→red→dark; colours depend on temperature and lighting, not a universal chronology for all magmas.

questions.prompt: Name the two types of crust that form tectonic plates.
questions.explanation: Oceanic and continental crust; tectonic plates also include uppermost mantle.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of transform boundary?
options: Sundra trench between Australia and Indonesia.
questions.explanation: South Island New Zealand includes the transform-dominated Alpine Fault, with oblique convergence as well.

questions.prompt: Which scale is used to measure the magnitude of earthquakes?
questions.explanation: Richter is the only real earthquake magnitude scale listed; modern large-event reports commonly use moment magnitude.

questions.prompt: What is pyroclastic flow?
options: The upward expulsion of lava during a volcanic eruption.
The varying constituents between tectonic plates.
A cloud of ash, rock and gas at about 500 degrees celsius.
questions.explanation: C is closest: a fast-moving ground-hugging flow of hot gas, ash and fragments. Temperature is variable, not fixed500°C.

sci-repo-y10-sby-2018-earth-mc-1.title: Year 10 Science — Universe,climate and Earth systems — SafetyBay2018 (original source MC)
sci-repo-y10-sby-2018-earth-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: The most widely accepted theory that explains where our universe came from is
options: The Infinite and Steady State theory.
questions.explanation: Big Bang theory describes a hot, dense early universe and subsequent expansion.

questions.prompt: Hubble observed that galaxies are
questions.explanation: Most distant galaxies show recession/redshift associated with expansion; bound nearby galaxies can approach.

questions.prompt: What is Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) Radiation?
options: Leftover heat from the Big Bang.
questions.explanation: CMB is relic radiation from the hot early universe, not literal residual warmth of an explosion into pre-existing space.

questions.prompt: What was the force that allowed galaxies to form in the early universe?
questions.explanation: Gravity amp lif ied density differences to form galaxies.

questions.prompt: The Biosphere depends on which three other spheres?
questions.explanation: Lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere interact with the biosphere.

questions.prompt: Most of the water that gets into the atmosphere comes from large bodies of water on Earth. This water gets into the atmosphere because of:
questions.explanation: Evaporation transfers water from large water bodies to the atmosphere.

questions.prompt: Global warming affects sea levels. Which of these is a likely consequence if the trend of global warming continues in coming decades?
options: Melting glaciers will cause flash flooding in mountainous regions.
Melting glaciers will cause flooding of coastal towns and cities.
Evaporation will cause sea levels to drop enlarging coastal areas.
Evaporation will cause the formation of U-shaped valleys.
questions.explanation: B. Rising seas from land-ice melt/thermal expansion increase coastal-flood risk; mountain glacial flooding can also occur but is not the sea-level consequence asked.

questions.prompt: Other than melting land-based ice sheets, which of these factors has made the largest contribution to the rise in sea level over the past 100 years?
questions.explanation: A. Warming water expands, contributing substantially to sea-level rise; melting floating sea ice has little direct sea-level effect.

questions.prompt: Which of these is the greatest threat to the survival of an ecosystem?
options: Less organisms at higher levels of the food web.
A shrinking variety of animal and plant species.
questions.explanation: C. Loss of biodiversity can undermine ecosystem resilience; other options describe normal ecosystem features.

sci-repo-y10-sby-2016-forensic-mc-1.title: Year 10 Science — Forensic science source test —2016paper (original source MC)
sci-repo-y10-sby-2016-forensic-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: The word Forensic comes from the word FORENSIS which comes from
questions.explanation: Forensis is Latin, relating to the forum/public proceedings.

questions.prompt: To be a good eyewitness, a person should be:
questions.explanation: Alert and observant; eyewitness memory can still be unreliable.

questions.prompt: Small items of evidence left at crime scenes are:
questions.explanation: Contact/trace evidence.

questions.prompt: Ballistics is the study of:
questions.explanation: Ballistics studies projectiles/firearms and their motion/effects.

questions.prompt: Who proposed the ‘Exchange Theory’ in 1910?
questions.explanation: Edmond Locard is associated with the exchange principle.

questions.prompt: The unusual microscope used by forensic laboratories is the   _____________ microscope.
questions.explanation: Comparison microscope permits side-by-side comparison; forensic laboratories also use many other types.

questions.prompt: Which of the fibres below are natural?
questions.explanation: Linen is natural flax fibre; rayon is regenerated manufactured cellulose.

questions.prompt: The instrument used to study fibres in detail is:
questions.explanation: Microscope.

questions.prompt: Regarding fingerprints, which one is the odd word below?
questions.explanation: Delta is a feature within some fingerprint patterns, while arch, loop, whorl are major pattern classes.

questions.prompt: The most common type of fingerprint pattern is:
questions.explanation: Loops are the most common broad fingerprint pattern class in the standard teaching distribution.

questions.prompt: How much blood does an average adult have in their body?
questions.explanation: About5–6L is the listed classroom estimate; adult blood volume varies with body size and other factors.

questions.prompt: Blood is a complex mixture of four main components. Red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets and   _________________?
questions.explanation: Plasma is the liquid component.

questions.prompt: Name the person credited with the discovery of DNA profiling:
questions.explanation: Alec Jeffreys developed DNA fingerprinting/profiling.

questions.prompt: Name the substance that is not produced by sweat glands:
questions.explanation: Oil/sebum is mainly from sebaceous rather than sweat glands.

sci-repo-y10-sby-2017-sport-mc-1.title: Year 10 Science — Sport science —SafetyBay2017 (original source MC)
sci-repo-y10-sby-2017-sport-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a skill related component of fitness?
questions.explanation: Muscular endurance is usually health-related, whereas agility, speed, power are classified as skill-related in this source.

questions.prompt: Which component of fitness is measured in the “Beep Test?”
questions.explanation: Beep/shuttle run test estimates cardiorespiratory endurance.

questions.prompt: The plyometric training method focuses on which component of fitness?
questions.explanation: Plyometric training focuses on rapid force/power development.

questions.prompt: How many bones make up the adult skeleton?
questions.explanation: 206is the conventional adult count, with normal anatomical variation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a type of bone?
questions.explanation: Wide is not a standard basic bone-shape class.

questions.prompt: The Olympics have banned the practice of “blood doping” in athletes, as it causes an unfair advantage. Blood doping increases which constituent of blood?
questions.explanation: Increased red-cell mass can increase oxygen carrying capacity; the item is about mechanism, not an endorsement of blood doping.

questions.prompt: The shoulder is an example of which type of joint?
questions.explanation: Shoulder joint is synovial, more particularly ball-and-socket.

questions.prompt: Being extremely flexible in a joint is referred to as being “double jointed.” Which of the following is NOT a medical term for being double jointed?
questions.explanation: Hypertensile is not the listed hypermobile/hyperextensible joint term.
